prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it answers this question: how many orders did Voltmarkt take in each ISO week, for the orders from 2025-12-15 to 2025-12-31? Use the orders table. order_ts holds the time of the order in UTC, so work in UTC and keep the orders from 2025-12-15 00:00 up to but not including 2026-01-01 00:00. Return three columns, in this order: iso_year, the year the ISO week belongs to, iso_week, the ISO week number, and orders, the number of orders. Return one row for each ISO week. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, look at the iso_year column: one row says week 1 of 2025, but its days are at the end of December 2025.
Monday 29 December 2025 starts ISO week 1 of 2026. year() gives the calendar year of each day; the ISO week needs the year the week belongs to.
starter_sql:
SELECT year(order_ts) AS iso_year, week(order_ts) AS iso_week, COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders
WHERE order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-12-15 00:00:00'
  AND order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
GROUP BY year(order_ts), week(order_ts)
why_this_works: isoyear gives the year the ISO week belongs to, so 29 to 31 December 2025 show as week 1 of 2026, not week 1 of 2025.
